Radiographs (Figure 2, Figure 3a–c, Figure 4a, Figure 5a and Figure 6a) are often the initial imaging modality in a patient suspected of having gout, as they are readily accessible and inexpensive. Caption describes erosions with a sclerotic border and overhanging edges in the heads of both first metatarsal bones; the in-text text calls these typical gout features.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Transverse native CT of both feet demonstrates the captioned higher-density zone at the lateral margin of the right Achilles tendon, supported in the text by MSU crystal deposition on DECT, a specific manifestation of gout. B: Color-coded dual-energy CT directly shows MSU crystal deposition in the Achilles tendon, a characteristic gout manifestation. C: Coronal CT demonstrates bilateral first MTP erosions with sclerotic margins and overhanging edges, characteristic radiographic manifestations of gout.

in_text_mentions: The native CT images showed erosions with a sclerotic border and overhanging edges in the MTP-I of both feet and a higher-density zone in the lateral margin of the Achilles tendon of his right foot with MSU crystal deposition on DECT, all typical features seen in gout [5] (Figure 1).
